sources.citation: Teng 2008, A Reference Grammar of Puyuma (PL-595), sec. 2.4-2.4.2 (ANU repository full read)
sources.quote: Word stress in Puyuma falls on the last syllable, and is thus non-phonemic. ... An affix counts as part of the word in stress assignment, but a clitic does not. Because stress is word-final, stress is diagnostic only for suffixes and enclitics.

sources.citation: Teng, Stacy Fang-ching. 2008. A reference grammar of Puyuma, an Austronesian language of Taiwan (Pacific Linguistics 595). Canberra: Pacific Linguistics, ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-595 (ANU Open Research, CC-BY 4.0).
sources.quote: 'Word stress in Puyuma falls on the last syllable, and is thus non-phonemic. Puyuma word stress is mainly marked by greater intensity, a higher pitch level, and longer duration.' (p.22) 'An affix counts as part of the word in stress assignment, but a clitic does not... beray [bəráj] -> tu=beray-ay [tubərajáj]... inaba [inabá] -> inaba=ku [inabáku]' (p.24). 2.4.2: 'The stress of the final word in an interrogative sentence is shifted from the last syllable to the penultimate syllable.' fn.18: ela is stressed on the first syllable, 'unlike most words, whose stress falls on the final position'.
